title: Video Repurposing from User Generated Content: A Large-scale Dataset and Benchmark (Repurpose-10K)
authors: Yongliang Wu; Wenbo Zhu; Jiawang Cao; et al.
venue: AAAI 2025 (Vol.39 No.8, pp.8487-8495 per repo BibTeX)
task_input: Untrimmed YouTube video (long-to-short; typically >30 min) as 1-s segments; CLIP ViT-B/32 + PANNs audio + WhisperX/MiniLM caption features
task_output: Set of ~60 s clips: per-1s binary select label + start/end offset regression; top-k (3 clips per 10 min) + soft-NMS
supervision_source: Implicit user behaviour on OpusClip (OPUS): LLM tool topic-segments video into coarse clips -> user marks like/post -> creator manually re-trims start/end; only re-edited clips kept
dataset_used_or_released: Released: Repurpose-10K = 8,398 videos from 114,883 creators (11,210 after splitting >30 min), 120,925 clips, 4,539.94 h; train/val/test 8/1/1 JSON splits in GitHub; videos must be fetched with yt-dlp
video_length_scale: chunks <=30 min (mean ~20 min, max 1800 s) of 8,399 YouTube videos; paper: avg 0.54 h, 4,539.94 h (JSON timeRange sums to 3,803 h [V])
eval_metrics: tIoU@0.5-0.9 + Avg (threshold 0.5, soft-NMS, k=3 clips/10 min per paper); human Engagement/Completeness 1-5 (10 raters) on label sources only; no boundary-specific or self-containedness metric
key_result_with_number: Avg tIoU 11.57 (24.94/16.35/10.14/4.86/1.57 at 0.5-0.9) vs QD-DETR(V&A) 10.16; ablation A 9.66 V 9.52 C 9.59 A&V 10.31 A&V&C 10.75 full 11.57; released JSON: 120,942 clips/11,211 chunks, clip median ~36 s (98% in 15-90 s), 5.3 clips per 10 min, 29-30% of chunk time selected; 807 YouTube ids span >1 split (404 train&test)
code_available: Yes: github.com/yongliang-wu/Repurpose (MIT per GitHub API); annotations only (train/val/test JSON), videos via yt-dlp, no features released
license: Code MIT; no dataset licence in paper/README [V]; underlying YouTube videos + OpusClip user edits
reading_depth: full-text (arXiv HTML v2 all sections) + repo README + released train/val/test JSON parsed (own statistics)
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Closest existing long-to-short benchmark with real user-curated and re-trimmed clips; labels come from OpusClip's own candidate generator (selection bias [I]); absolute tIoU is very low (~11.6) and self-containedness is only judged by a 1-5 human Completeness rating, no automatic metric.

title: From Long Videos to Engaging Clips: A Human-Inspired Video Editing Framework with Multimodal Narrative Understanding (HIVE / DramaAD)
authors: Xiangfeng Wang; Xiao Li; Yadong Wei; et al.
task_input: Short-drama episodes concatenated into 20-30 min storylines (~10 episodes); ASR corrected by OCR subtitles + diarization + face clustering + MLLM scene narration
task_output: Several edited videos: LLM-chosen highlight scenes + (opening,ending) scene pairs + pruned scenes; boundaries are scene-level not second-level
supervision_source: No training; prompted DeepSeek-R1 / GPT-4o / Gemini; references = 522 professionally edited ad videos (~30 min each, paid editors)
dataset_used_or_released: DramaAD on HF: paper says 3,104 videos (2,582 drama + 522 ads), 68 h; HF listing shows 2,603 raw_videos + 501 edited_videos + script.json/narration json per drama; arXiv abstract page says 800+ episodes (inconsistent)
video_length_scale: dramas ~40 min each (Fig.2 caption); episodes 1-3 min; test storylines 20-30 min
eval_metrics: Human-viewer Diversity (1-mean pairwise IoU), Smoothness (min per interruption), Engagement (share at 1x speed), VEI=Eng x Smooth, Hook Rate, Suspense Rate; rater count/agreement not stated [V]
key_result_with_number: Table 2 VEI HIVE 4.01 vs End2End(ASR) 0.54 / End2End(narration) 1.14 / human 6.35; Hook 0.71 / Susp 0.73 vs human 0.87 / 0.91; w/o boundary selection Hook 0.28 Susp 0.30; w/o highlight Eng 0.62; ASR-vs-narration comparison confounded with segmentation
code_available: No code repo found; prompts in appendix; dataset on HF (wonderful9462/DramaAD)
license: HF dataset has no licence tag [V]; paper: data authorised by copyright holders for academic research
reading_depth: full-text (arXiv HTML v2 incl. appendix prompts) + HF dataset file listing
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Only industrial paper with an explicit pipeline for opening/ending (boundary) selection and a prompt rule against openings that rely on prior context; but domain is short drama, human eval size not reported, and arXiv abstract says 800+ episodes vs 2,582 in body (inconsistent).

title: Vidi2.5: Large Multimodal Models for Video Understanding and Creation
authors: Vidi Team; Chia-Wen Kuo; Chuang Huang; et al.
venue: arXiv preprint (report updated Jan 2026 per repo); venue [V]
task_input: Raw video up to 30-60+ min; Highlight mode needs no query
task_output: Highlight mode: multiple highlight segments + concise titles (shown only as qualitative Fig.8); TR: time ranges; STG: tubes; Vidi-Edit: structured editing plan
supervision_source: SFT + RL with verifiable rewards; human-annotated data for RL; LLM-judge rewards for Think model
dataset_used_or_released: Released: VUE-STG (982 videos, 204.79 h), VUE-TR-V2 (847 videos, 310.7 h), VUE-PLOT
modalities: vision (1 fps) + audio (16 kHz) + text; GPT-5 baseline had no audio and 120-frame cap
eval_metrics: TR: AUC of temporal precision/recall/IoU (integer-second timestamps); STG: vIoU, tIoU; PLOT: accuracy, speaker IoU, WER; no metric for highlight+title extraction
key_result_with_number: VUE-TR-V2 IoU-AUC overall Vidi2.5 49.62 / Vidi2 48.75 / Gemini 3 Pro 37.58 / GPT-5 17.15; >60 min 42.22 / 38.65 / 21.19 / 12.49; by query modality (Vidi2.5) audio 45.64, vision 52.77, vision+audio 47.65; highlight+title extraction only qualitative (Fig. 8)
code_available: Yes: github.com/bytedance/vidi (eval scripts, annotations, Vidi1.5-9B weights + finetune code; 12B Vidi2/2.5 weights not confirmed [V])
license: GitHub NOASSERTION, no LICENSE file found [V]
reading_depth: sections:abstract,intro,model overview,benchmarks (STG/TR-V2/PLOT),TR+STG+PLOT results,highlight-application paragraph,Vidi-Edit (arXiv HTML) + Vidi-1 overview/results + repo README; appendix baseline prompts and QA tables not read
one_line_takeaway: Answers (c): the 'highlight clips + title' capability exists in the product/demo but the report gives no quantitative evaluation of clip extraction, boundary quality or engagement.

title: Mr. HiSum: A Large-scale Dataset for Video Highlight Detection and Summarization
authors: Jinhwan Sul; Jihoon Han; Joonseok Lee
task_input: YouTube-8M 1 fps Inception-v3 PCA-1024 visual features of 2-5 min videos
task_output: Frame/shot importance (Most Replayed score); top-15%/50% 5 s shots as highlights; KTS shots + 0/1 knapsack 15% summary
supervision_source: YouTube 'Most replayed' heatmap aggregated over >=50,000 viewers; 100 normalised bins per video aligned to 1 fps
dataset_used_or_released: Released: 31,892 videos, 1,788 h, 3,509 YT8M entity labels; metadata + labels + crawler on GitHub (features need YT8M download)
video_length_scale: 121-300 s, avg 201.9 s; music category excluded
eval_metrics: Highlight: MAP at top-15%/50% of 5-s shots; summarisation: F1 with KTS + 0/1 knapsack (15% budget); label validity: cross-dataset transfer (TVSum, SumMe, YouTube Highlights) and 30-rater user study; no boundary metric
key_result_with_number: PGL-SUM F1 55.89 / MAP50 61.60 / MAP15 27.45 (2,000 test videos); user study 64.8% agree / 15.6% neutral / 19.6% disagree; SL-module TVSum MAP target 71.3 vs zero-shot 69.5 vs fine-tuned 73.0; >=1,000 validation videos needed; authors admit self-fulfilling replay bias and undefined partial-replay counting
code_available: Yes: github.com/MRHiSum/MR.HiSum (labels via Google Drive h5, crawler, baselines, checkpoints)
license: Dataset CC BY 4.0 following YouTube-8M + YouTube ToS (README); code academic non-commercial (LICENSE); GitHub field other
reading_depth: full-text (paper PDF text layer, all sections; no appendix in PDF) + GitHub README/DATASET.md/LICENSE
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Canonical Most-Replayed supervision; authors themselves flag self-fulfilling bias (UI shows heatmap after 50k views) and unclear partial-replay counting; only 2-5 min visual-only videos, so says nothing about hour-long speech content or boundaries.

title: SVHighlights: Towards Extremely Long Sport Video Highlight Detection
authors: Donggyu Lee; Youngbin Ki; Jeonghun Kang; et al.
venue: KDD 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (DOI 10.1145/3770855.3817564 per repo README)
task_input: Full-length sports broadcast (>1 h; avg 2.00 h; 8 sports)
task_output: Saliency per 2 s clip -> ranked/selected highlight clips (HIT@K, IoU)
supervision_source: Official full broadcast <-> official highlight video pairs; PSNR frame matching + temporal-consistency rule + automatic filter (PSNR<20) + manual binary check (changes 3.7% of frames)
dataset_used_or_released: Released (URLs + extracted features + labels; no video redistribution): 320 videos, 640.18 h, 40 per sport
eval_metrics: mAP, HIT@1, HIT@K (K=#GT clips per video), IoU over 2-s clips; appendix window-based event F1; label validity Likert user study (10 raters, 120 clips, Krippendorff alpha per sport)
key_result_with_number: Table 7: TF-Selector mAP 12.81 / HIT@1 26.56 / HIT@K 16.90 / IoU 10.58 vs TR-DETR 12.72/24.06/12.86/7.09, TRACE mAP 23.14 but IoU 7.63; Table 10 caption-only HIT@1 15.00 -> +audio volume 16.25 -> +transcript 21.25 -> all 26.56; labels: PSNR 26.74 / SSIM 0.865 / CLIP 0.955 alignment, manual check changes 3.7% of frames; user study positives 3.42 vs negatives 1.94/1.97 (alpha 0.22-0.72 by sport); project page quotes +3.12 HIT@1 vs arXiv text +2.50
code_available: Yes: github.com/leedongkyu2019/SVHighlights (TF-Selector + preprocessing code, Apache-2.0 per GitHub API)
license: Dataset CC BY-NC 4.0 (HF card; annotations+features, no videos); code Apache-2.0; paper CC BY 4.0
reading_depth: full-text (arXiv HTML v2 incl. appendices) + project page + GitHub README + HF dataset card
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Cleanest example of official-full <-> official-highlight pairs as label source, with scalable alignment and a modality ablation; sports only and no self-containedness or boundary-quality notion (labels at 2 s).

title: TVHighlights: LLM-Guided Human-Free Collaborative Training for Video Highlight Detection in Movies and TV Dramas
authors: Qi Qiu; Xuan Wu; Jiawei Peng; et al.
task_input: Movie/TV-drama SHORT videos (train avg 50.6 s, test avg 134.9 s) split into 2 s clips; CLIP ViT-L-14 + SlowFast visual, ImageBind audio
task_output: Per-clip highlight score (query-agnostic)
supervision_source: Train: video fingerprinting traces popular short-form reuses (platform titles filtered by LLM) back to source videos; reuse frequency = community vote; test: multi-annotator 2 s majority vote
dataset_used_or_released: TVHighlights: 1,721 videos in 15 genres (train 1,368 with reuse-vote-derived video-level labels; test 353 = 171 highlight + 182 non-highlight, human 2-s majority vote); release promised after anonymisation, not yet public
video_length_scale: SHORT videos: raw short-form avg 248.8 s (4,767), train 1,368 videos avg 50.6 s, test 353 videos avg 134.9 s (supplement Table A); not hour-long
eval_metrics: AUC, AP (clip level, overall and per category), mAP on YouTube Highlights, Cohen kappa of generated vs human labels; no boundary/IoU metric
key_result_with_number: LTV-HD Stage2 AUC 92.74 / AP 71.20 vs Qwen-vl-max per-clip scoring 88.40/47.42, per-clip MR 64.80/36.62, UMT 60.50/45.13 (row order inferred), Stage1 87.34/62.39; Emotion AP 60.00 vs 41.38; supp: swapping LLM (Claude-opus-4-5) 93.78/72.92
code_available: No code URL in paper or supplement [V]
license: Not stated; underlying movie/TV clip copyright unstated [V]
reading_depth: sections:main paper (abstract,intro,dataset,method,experiments,ablation tables) + supplementary (dataset stats, MLLM prompts, LLM sensitivity, runtime); no arXiv/HTML version
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Second example of reuse-in-short-video (user-made clip) frequency as supervision, here via fingerprint matching; domain is cinematic and labels are noisy popularity votes, but shows how to turn downstream reuse into clip-level labels.

title: A Multimodal Transformer for Live Streaming Highlight Prediction (KuaiHL / KLive)
authors: Jiaxin Deng; Shiyao Wang; Dong Shen; et al.
venue: arXiv preprint; repo name suggests ICME 2024 (venue [V])
task_input: Causal look-back window of 20 x 30 s live segments: 3 frames + streamer ASR + audience comments + streamer ID
task_output: Predicted per-segment Long View Through Rate (LVTR) for the next segment
supervision_source: Implicit viewer feedback: LVTR = share of impressions with long viewing time (weak supervision); Border-aware pairwise loss
dataset_used_or_released: KLive: 17,897 live rooms, 19,334 h, 1,436,979 train / 286,510 test samples; release promised, GitHub repos are placeholders [V]
eval_metrics: Kendall tau on LVTR; mAP on PHD
key_result_with_number: tau 0.5961; ablation: w/o text(ASR+comments) -2.01%, w/o visual -4.72%, w/o streamer ID -0.51%; border-aware pair loss +1.11%, + alignment +2.0% total
license: Paper CC BY 4.0; dataset/code license none [V]
one_line_takeaway: Platform-scale implicit-feedback labels (view time) for live highlights with a quantified modality ablation, but labels are tied to recommender impressions (exposure/position confound not discussed [I]) and data is not actually public.

title: AntPivot: Livestream Highlight Detection via Hierarchical Attention Mechanism
authors: Yang Zhao; Xuan Lin; Wenqiang Xu; et al.
venue: arXiv preprint only (no venue comment on arXiv page) [V]
task_input: Long Chinese finance/insurance livestream recording: ASR utterance sequence + speaker id + mel 'pattern' embedding
task_output: Non-overlapping (start,end) highlight proposals whose boundaries are utterance boundaries; per-utterance highlight confidence + boundary probability decoded by dynamic programming
supervision_source: 10 human annotators watched whole streams and marked start/end of 'valuable segments with an integral topic and complete content' (incl. Q&A)
dataset_used_or_released: Released: AntHighlight = 3,655 livestreams, 2,861.55 h; splits 3055/100/500; avg 9.60 highlights per stream; avg 211.87 s per highlight; avg 298.58 utterances/stream; download link in repo (Aliyun drive)
video_length_scale: avg ~47 min per stream (2,861.55 h / 3,655); highlights ~7.65% of stream
eval_metrics: AP at tIoU 0.5-0.9; Boundary F1 for start and end (hit if |delta|<5 s; GT segments <10 s discarded)
key_result_with_number: S+K+P AP@0.5 68.9 / @0.9 36.0, F1 start/end 44.5/48.9; S only 67.2/34.6, 42.2/45.1; S+K 43.2/46.8; S+P 43.3/46.2; decoding: threshold 36.8/42.2, greedy 42.8/44.7, DP 44.5/48.9; no external baselines; no inter-annotator agreement reported
code_available: Yes: github.com/ContentTech/AntPivot (Apache-2.0 per GitHub API); data via Aliyun Drive link in README (not opened)
license: Code Apache-2.0; data licence not stated [V]
reading_depth: sections:abstract,intro,related work,Sec3 method (representation, Pivot Transformer, DP inference),Sec4 dataset+metrics+all result tables (ar5iv HTML); supplementary not available
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Closest precedent for boundary-as-structured-prediction on long speech video: candidate cut points are utterance boundaries, explicit boundary F1, DP decoding, 'complete topic' definition; but 200 s segments, one finance domain, human boundaries, no engagement signal and no hook title.

title: PodReels: Human-AI Co-Creation of Video Podcast Teasers
authors: Sitong Wang; Zheng Ning; Anh Truong; et al.
task_input: Hour-long video podcast episode: word-timed transcript, active-speaker diarization, filler words, audio events; user criteria (length 15/30/45 s, speaker, style, keywords)
task_output: Candidate 15-45 s teaser moments as sentence-ID sets (GPT-4) + tagline; user refines with before/after sentence windows
supervision_source: No trained supervision; formative study of audience comments + creator interviews (design criteria: strong hook, clear context, brevity); annotators check LLM adherence to criteria
dataset_used_or_released: No dataset released; formative study 7 teasers/10 listeners/5 creators; technical eval on 4 YouTube trending episodes (~45 min avg), 168 single-param + 30 multi-param clips
video_length_scale: hour-long podcast episodes in formative study; technical eval on 4 episodes avg ~45 min
modalities: ASR text + diarization + filler words + audio events (no ablation)
eval_metrics: LLM criterion-adherence accuracy (duration +-5 s; style/keyword 1-7 rating, kappa .61/.63, >=5 = match); within-subjects user study n=10 (time, NASA-TLX, CSI, SUS)
key_result_with_number: Single-param adherence duration 86.1 / speaker 88.9 / keyword 87.5 / style 77.1 (funny 41.7); multi-param 76.7% of 30 clips right on >=3 of 4 criteria; user study n=10: abstract says 59% of time and 44% of mental demand but Discussion says -41% mental demand and -56% time (inconsistent)
code_available: No code or release link found in paper [V]
license: Paper arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive licence; no data/code licence
reading_depth: sections:abstract,intro,related work,formative study 3.1-3.4,system 4,technical eval 5,user-study design+summary,discussion/limitations,appendix prompts (per-measure user-study tables not extracted)
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Nearest neighbour on domain+task for spoken podcasts: formative study explicitly names 'clear context / self-contained' and unresolved referents ('here','them') as failure, uses sentence as the edit unit and context-window refinement; but human-in-the-loop tool, no engagement labels, no benchmark, no boundary metric.

title: RankCut: A Ranking-Based LLM Approach to Extractive Summarization for Transcript-Based Video Editing
authors: Sana Shah; Mackenzie Leake; Kun Chu; et al.
task_input: Transcripts of long interviews / lectures / meetings
task_output: Strictly extractive time-aligned transcript spans under a duration budget, shown as priority markers on a timeline

title: Video2GIF: Automatic Generation of Animated GIFs from Video
authors: Michael Gygli; Yale Song; Liangliang Cao
task_input: Video segments with C3D features
task_output: Ranked list of segments by suitability as GIF (mean GIF 5.8 s)
supervision_source: User-made GIFs aligned to source videos by perceptual-hash frame matching; unselected segments as negatives; Robust Deep RankNet with adaptive Huber rank loss for web noise
dataset_used_or_released: Video2GIF dataset: 121,647 GIFs, 84,754 videos, 7,379 h (experiments: 100,699 GIFs / 70,456 videos; test 357 videos); only 432 videos CC-BY
eval_metrics: nMSD, mAP
key_result_with_number: nMSD ~44% and mAP ~16% across Huber-rank variants (Table 2; best row not isolated) [V]

license: Only 432 videos CC-BY; rest follows source sites [F: Table 1]
one_line_takeaway: Earliest large 'user-made short clip <-> long source' supervision; shows noisy-label handling (Huber rank loss) but no sound, no speech, 5.8 s GIFs, and dataset is partly defunct.

title: Towards Extracting Highlights From Recorded Live Videos: An Implicit Crowdsourcing Approach (LIGHTOR)
authors: Ruochen Jiang; Changbo Qu; Jiannan Wang; et al.
task_input: Recorded Twitch live videos (0.5-2 h) + timestamped chat; later viewers' play/seek interactions
task_output: Highlight start/end positions (seconds to <1 min) refined iteratively
supervision_source: Chat message number/length/similarity predicts approximate position; viewer interaction data (play, seek) refines boundaries; labels: experienced players (Dota2) / YouTube highlight collections matching (LoL)
dataset_used_or_released: Dota2: 60 Twitch videos; LoL: 173 videos from NACLS; code+reproducibility at github.com/sfu-db/Lightor_Exp
eval_metrics: Chat Precision@K; Video Precision@K start (correct if within [s-10,e]) / end ([s,e+10])
key_result_with_number: Chat-only features handle the reaction delay (chat lags the event); generalises LoL->Dota2 with 1 training video; deep chat-LSTM baseline needs far more data (numbers not isolated) [V]
one_line_takeaway: Shows chat/interaction signals are lagged and noisy and need explicit boundary refinement; gaming domain, 10 s tolerance, not speech-centred.

title: Video Highlight Prediction Using Audience Chat Reactions
authors: Cheng-Yang Fu; Joon Lee; Mohit Bansal; et al.
task_input: LoL championship Twitch VOD frames (5 s window) and audience chat (7 s window; English + Traditional Chinese)
task_output: Per-frame highlight probability
supervision_source: Community-made highlight videos (single YouTube channel, 5-7 min each) aligned to full matches by template matching; last 25% of each highlight clip used as positives
dataset_used_or_released: 321 matches (218 NALCS + 103 LMS); dataset stated 'will be released' [V]
eval_metrics: frame-level F-score
key_result_with_number: Test F-score NALCS/LMS: chat-only 43.2/39.7, video-only 72.2/69.2, chat+video 74.7/70.0 (+2.5/+0.8 over video)
one_line_takeaway: Early quantified chat-vs-video ablation (chat alone weak, adds little on top of vision); also observes the 'action' sits late in the highlight clip so context precedes it.

title: Video Highlights Detection and Summarization with Lag-Calibration based on Concept-Emotion Mapping of Crowd-sourced Time-Sync Comments
authors: Qing Ping; Chaomei Chen
venue: EMNLP 2017 Workshop on New Frontiers in Summarization
task_input: Bilibili time-sync comments (danmaku) per shot
task_output: Shot-level highlight scores / summaries

dataset_used_or_released: Released: danmu embeddings from 2,108,746 comments / 6,368 long videos, emotion lexicon, danmu of 11 evaluation videos (GitHub)
eval_metrics: Highlight and summary evaluation vs gold (see paper)
key_result_with_number: abstract-level: comments lag the shot, sparse/noisy, highlights subjective; numbers not read [V]

title: From Understanding to Engagement: Personalized pharmacy Video Clips via Vision Language Models (VLMs)
authors: Suyash Mishra; Qiang Li; Srikanth Patil; et al.

title: Vidi: Large Multimodal Models for Video Understanding and Editing (VUE-TR benchmark)
authors: Vidi Team (ByteDance) et al. [individual authors not extracted: V]
task_input: long video (1 fps) + audio (16 kHz) + text query (keyword/phrase/sentence; vision/audio/both)
task_output: one or MULTIPLE time ranges as generated timestamps
supervision_source: synthetic stitched captioned videos + 1M real long videos with LMM dense captions and sentence-level subtitles (>30M pairs); training clips pre-segmented at 5-30 s by scene-boundary detection + subtitle punctuation; two-round human annotation for retrieval post-training
dataset_used_or_released: releases VUE-TR: 1598 queries / 428 videos / 107 h
eval_metrics: IoU/precision/recall over unions of multiple time ranges; AUC over threshold sweep [0,1] as primary; accuracy-threshold curves (IoU@0.5 etc.); no multi-reference, no judge
key_result_with_number: VUE-TR Table 3 (AUC x100; Vidi-1.5 / Vidi / Gemini-2.0-Flash / Gemini-2.5-Pro / GPT-4o): overall IoU 39.6/35.4/21.2/15.2/13.6; P 55.3/49.0/40.3/39.3/25.9; R 54.8/52.5/34.6/28.9/24.0; IoU by duration <1min 58.4/54.6/49.2/42.6/32.5 down to >60min 32.3/27.5/2.9/2.4/9.5; Gemini evaluated at 256px for long videos, GPT-4o capped at 120 frames
code_available: project page bytedance.github.io/vidi-website; 'released Vidi models' per Sec 7; repo URL and weights not seen in text
license: not stated in text read; arXiv page = arXiv perpetual licence (paper only)
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Closest benchmark for multi-answer long-video time-range retrieval; its threshold-swept IoU-AUC is a ready-made tolerance-free boundary metric, but boundaries are still free-form generated timestamps (candidate snapping only appears in training-data segmentation).

title: TimeLens: Rethinking Video Temporal Grounding with Multimodal LLMs
authors: Jun Zhang, Teng Wang, Yuying Ge et al.
task_input: video + one text query
task_output: single segment (start,end) as text timestamps
supervision_source: GRPO RLVR with temporal-IoU reward (thinking-free); SFT/RL compared; data re-annotated: manual (benchmarks) and Gemini-2.5-Pro (training)
dataset_used_or_released: releases TimeLens-Bench (re-annotated Charades-STA/ActivityNet-Captions/QVHighlights) and TimeLens-100K (~20K videos, ~100K annotations)
video_length_scale: mostly <= few minutes (Charades ~30 s; ANet/QVH longer; exact table V)
eval_metrics: R1@{0.3,0.5,0.7}, mIoU on 3 re-annotated benchmarks (4,279 videos, avg 107.8 s, 9,404 annotations); no IoU 0.9, no second-level error; no multi-reference or judge
key_result_with_number: Table 5: training on original noisy data Charades R1@0.7 14.0 / mIoU 35.6 vs TimeLens-100K 28.1 / 48.3 (label quality doubles R1@0.7); Table 1 mIoU Charades/ANet/QVH: TimeLens-8B 55.2/53.2/65.5, Gemini-2.5-Pro 52.8/58.1/70.4 (TimeLens-8B does NOT beat Pro on ANet/QVH), GPT-5 40.5/42.9/56.8; Table 3 thinking-free RLVR (1.0x) 48.3/43.1/56.7 vs SFT-100K (2.4x) 48.6/39.7/49.0; timestamps emitted as text with 0.1 s resolution
code_available: paper says code/data/models 'will be released'; project site timelens-arc-lab.github.io; repo not confirmed
license: paper CC BY 4.0; dataset/model licence not confirmed; derived from datasets whose licences may restrict redistribution
reading_depth: full-text (arxiv.org/html v2, Sec 1-6, App B/C/D/E/F/H, Tables 1-5)
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Shows that boundary-annotation quality (not only model design) dominates grounding scores and re-ranks models; provides the strongest tIoU-RLVR recipe, but it only reports up to IoU 0.7 and compares only continuous text-timestamp variants.

title: Time-R1: Post-Training Large Vision Language Model for Temporal Video Grounding
authors: Ye Wang, Ziheng Wang, Boshen Xu et al.
task_input: video + query
task_output: (thinking trace +) single [t_s,t_e]
supervision_source: GRPO with tIoU reward + template reward; TimeRFT (~2.5K curated samples, Gaussian difficulty filtering, multi-epoch)
dataset_used_or_released: releases TVGBench (800 instances from Charades-STA, ActivityNet, HiREST, EgoNLQ, TaCoS)
eval_metrics: R1@{0.3,0.5,0.7}, mIoU; video QA accuracy (MVBench, TempCompass, EgoSchema, VideoMME long)
key_result_with_number: Table 1 R1@0.3/0.5/0.7: Charades-STA 78.1/60.8/35.3, ActivityNet 58.6/39.0/21.4, TVGBench 41.8/29.4/16.4 (2.5K RL samples); Table 2: tIoU reward alone does not help (R1@0.7 12.9 vs 13.2 baseline), tIoU+multi-epoch 16.4 vs multi-epoch alone 14.2; reward tIoU = IoU*(1-|dts|/t)*(1-|dte|/t)
code_available: project page xuboshen.github.io/Time-R1; repo/weights not confirmed in text
license: not stated in text read; arXiv perpetual licence (paper only)
reading_depth: full-text (arxiv.org/html v3, Sec 1-5, Tables 1-2, App A/B)
one_line_takeaway: Origin of IoU-reward RL for grounding; authors themselves note IoU reward tolerates a boundary band epsilon, i.e. it optimises overlap not exact cut points.

title: How Should Video LLMs Output Time? An Analysis of Efficient Temporal Grounding Paradigms
authors: Shengji Jin, Yuanhao Zou, Victor Zhu et al.
task_input: video + query (32 frames, compact VLMs 0.5B-8B)
task_output: timestamps via text numerals / dedicated time tokens (TRACE-style) / continuous distribution head (DisTime-style)
supervision_source: controlled LoRA fine-tuning, identical data/backbones/protocol
dataset_used_or_released: uses Charades-STA, QVHighlights, YouCook2 (no new data)
eval_metrics: R1@0.5, R1@0.7, mIoU (Charades-STA, QVHighlights); mAP/HIT@1 (Gen. only); CIDEr/SODA_c/F1 (YouCook2); latency and parameter overhead; no IoU 0.9, no tolerance-window F1
key_result_with_number: Table 2 Charades-STA R1@.5/R1@.7/mIoU: SmolVLM2-0.5B Text 15.1/6.8/16.2 vs Cont. 41.8/22.5/43.4; Molmo2-8B Cont. mIoU 57.1 vs Text 27.5; 25% data Cont. 40.2 mIoU > Text 20.8 (100% data); Cont. 794 ms/query vs Gen. 1379 ms (2.2B). Confound: Cont. uses 1D-IoU+DFL loss, Text uses CE only; no candidate-selection arm
code_available: tg-paradigms.github.io (code and models stated public; not independently opened)
license: paper CC BY 4.0; datasets are existing public ones with their own licences
reading_depth: full-text (arxiv.org/html, Sec 1-6, Tables 2-4; appendix tables skimmed)
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Only controlled three-way ablation of how timestamps are emitted; all three paradigms regress free-form times, so there is still NO ablation against selecting among candidate cut points.

title: QVHighlights: Detecting Moments and Highlights in Videos via Natural Language Queries (Moment-DETR)
authors: Jie Lei, Tamara L. Berg, Mohit Bansal
task_input: pre-extracted video + query features
task_output: set of moments (center,width) + clip saliency; DETR decoder, no proposals/NMS
supervision_source: crowd annotation: 3 annotators per query for moments; 5-point saliency Likert
dataset_used_or_released: releases QVHighlights (>10,000 YouTube videos)
eval_metrics: R1@0.5/0.7; mAP@0.5/0.75/avg[0.5:0.95] for multi-moment; highlight mAP and HIT@1 (positive = Very Good)
key_result_with_number: ~90% of queries have mean pairwise IoU >0.9 among the 3 annotators; Moment-DETR vs proposal/span baseline XML+: R1@0.5 52.89 vs 46.69, but mAP@0.75 29.40 vs 34.67 (R1@0.7 33.02 vs 33.46) -> direct regression is better at loose, not strict, IoU; with ASR pretraining 59.78/40.33
one_line_takeaway: Canonical DETR-style regression + multi-moment mAP protocol; own results show regression weaker at strict IoU, the only in-house hint on the boundary-precision question.

title: Measure Twice, Cut Once: A Semantic-Oriented Approach to Video Temporal Localization with Video LLMs (MeCo)
authors: Zongshang Pang, Mayu Otani, Yuta Nakashima
task_input: video + query
task_output: video split into event/background segments by structural tokens (no timestamp tokens); target events read off the segmentation

dataset_used_or_released: standard temporal localization benchmarks (names V)
eval_metrics: standard grounding metrics (V)
key_result_with_number: abstract: outperforms timestamp-generation methods (numbers not read)
one_line_takeaway: Nearest thing to 'segment-then-select' in MLLMs, from the same lab as Otani 2019; a candidate-style alternative to timestamp regression worth deep-reading.

title: TimeLens2: Generalist Video Temporal Grounding with Multimodal LLMs
authors: Yuhan Zhu, Changlian Ma, Xiangyu Zeng et al.
task_input: video + query
task_output: variable-cardinality SET of evidence intervals

eval_metrics: mIoU on seven benchmarks
key_result_with_number: +14.2 / +13.0 / +18.1 mIoU over Qwen3-VL 2B/4B/8B backbones (abstract)
one_line_takeaway: Treats acceptable answers as interval SETS with a matching-free dense reward: closest published RL recipe for 'many answers acceptable'.

title: Towards One-to-Many Temporal Grounding (OMTG)
authors: Qi Xu, Yue Tan, Shihao Chen et al.

task_output: multiple segments
supervision_source: RL with temporal and caption rewards; 56k-sample curated dataset

key_result_with_number: abstract: EtF1 43.65%, +15.85 over Gemini 2.5 Pro and +15.61 over Seed-1.8; prior one-to-one MLLMs get near-zero scores
one_line_takeaway: Set-level (cardinality-aware) F1 for multiple acceptable segments - template for a set-level clip metric.

title: Grounding with Confidence: Controllable Generative Video Temporal Grounding
authors: Jinhao Chen, Benlei Cui, Ruijian Jia et al.
task_input: video + query
task_output: several candidate intervals each with a confidence score; threshold/budget selection

one_line_takeaway: Generate-then-score-and-select pattern with explicit accept/reject; relevant to ranking K clips.

title: A Survey on Temporal Sentence Grounding in Videos
authors: Xiaohan Lan, Yitian Yuan, Xin Wang et al.
task_output: survey of proposal-based vs proposal-free (regression / anchor-free / RL) grounding
eval_metrics: mIoU, R@n IoU@m with m in {0.3,0.5,0.7}
key_result_with_number: community uses m<=0.7; DiDeMo m=1 is only reachable by matching methods because GT is aggregated 5 s units; method families differ in many factors so no clean regression-vs-proposal ablation exists
one_line_takeaway: Used to substantiate that the regression-vs-candidate question has never been isolated; pre-LLM only.

title: Generic Event Boundary Detection: A Benchmark for Event Segmentation (Kinetics-GEBD)
authors: Mike Zheng Shou, Stan Weixian Lei, Weiyao Wang et al.

key_result_with_number: abstract-level only: benchmark with in-the-wild boundaries reflecting variation in human perception
code_available: annotations and baseline code released (LOVEU challenge)
one_line_takeaway: The standard tolerance-window boundary F1 protocol with multi-annotator handling; direct template for sentence/turn boundary F1.

title: VidChapters-7M: Video Chapters at Scale
authors: Antoine Yang, Arsha Nagrani, Ivan Laptev et al.

eval_metrics: recall/precision at time-distance and IoU tolerances (R@Ks/P@Ks; IoU in {0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9} per search summary: V); SODA_c
key_result_with_number: abstract-level only (numbers not read)
one_line_takeaway: Natural-supervision long-video boundary dataset using tolerance-based boundary P/R; the only boundary benchmark here that includes IoU 0.9 (V).

title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Video Summaries
authors: Mayu Otani, Yuta Nakashima, Esa Rahtu et al.

key_result_with_number: Table 1: TVSum avg F1 random 0.57 (KTS) / 0.58 (two-peak) vs human leave-one-out 0.54, DR-DSN 0.58, dppLSTM 0.60; SumMe max F1 random KTS 0.41 vs human 0.54, DR-DSN 0.41; Table 2 TVSum tau/rho human 0.177/0.204, dppLSTM 0.042/0.055, DR-DSN 0.020/0.026; human study 30 raters/pair: random vs DR-DSN 46% 'equally good/bad', random vs human -0.17
license: not stated; data are public SumMe/TVSum
reading_depth: full-text (ar5iv, Sec 1-6 + appendix; Table 1/2 checked cell by cell; figure bar values not read)
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Defines the 'many acceptable answers' failure of single-reference F1 and the segmentation-dominance problem - the origin of every later multi-reference / correlation protocol (and, for us, a warning that candidate segmentation drives scores).

title: Margin MCC: Chance-Robust Metric for Video Boundary Detection with Allowed Margin
authors: Kosuke Mizufune, Shunsuke Tanaka, Toshihide Yukitake et al.

task_output: metric
eval_metrics: Margin Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MMCC) vs F1 with allowed margin
key_result_with_number: abstract: even a completely random model gets inflated F1 when the number of predictions is large; MMCC designed so expected value for random guessing is zero, robust to over/under-segmentation (no numbers read)
code_available: not found (searched arXiv, GitHub via web search, author pages, Semantic Scholar)
license: Crossref lists CC-BY 4.0 for the paper (OA publishedVersion hosted only on dl.acm.org); no code found
reading_depth: abstract-only (full text not obtainable: ACM DL Cloudflare 403; no repository copy; Crossref metadata + 37-item reference list read)
one_line_takeaway: Recommend DEMOTE from core to background citation (abstract-level). Tolerance-window boundary F1 can be inflated by chance (random model with many predictions); MMCC is chance-corrected. No numbers, datasets or definitions verified.

title: Multi-Reference Evaluation of Dynamic Video Summaries Using Granule-Aware F-Measure
authors: Debashis Sen, V. K. Vivekraj

task_output: metric (GF-measure; GF(mad), GF(sat))

key_result_with_number: abstract: average F-measure is a special case; statistical, correlation and user studies on GF vs average/max F (numbers not read)
reading_depth: abstract-only (found via OpenAlex citations of Otani 2019)
one_line_takeaway: Multi-reference metric that explicitly models disagreement among references instead of avg/max.

title: How Good is a Video Summary? A New Benchmarking Dataset and Evaluation Framework Towards Realistic Video Summarization (VISIOCITY)
authors: Vishal Kaushal, Suraj Kothawade, Anshul Tomar et al.

reading_depth: abstract-only (found via OpenAlex citations of Otani 2019)
one_line_takeaway: Explicit 'several valid summaries' argument for long videos; metric details need deep read.

title: MEDit-Bench: A Dataset for Evaluating Message-Driven Narrative Video Editing
authors: Katsuya Ogata, Zongshang Pang, Mayu Otani
task_input: 7-18 min video + natural-language editing message

dataset_used_or_released: releases MEDit-Bench: 60 videos x 3 messages x 3 editors = 540 edits (YouTube IDs, messages, cut timestamps)
eval_metrics: union-tIoU R@{0.3,0.5,0.7}; cut-level greedy-matched F1@{0.3,0.5,0.7}; mIoU; LLM judge win rate (both orders); 1,620-evaluation human study; reward ablation Table 8
key_result_with_number: Human leave-one-out Table 3: R@0.3/0.5/0.7 0.432/0.133/0.033, F1@0.7 0.109; best model MEDitor-8B R@0.7 0.026; judge position swing 55.6% vs 20.2% = 35.4pp is App E text + Fig 8 (right), NOT Table 3; judge-vs-human agreement 59.9% (kappa 0.18, Pearson 0.185) on 540 triples (App E); 62.1% AI win (position-averaged) is App E text and conflicts with Table 3 Gemini-3-pro 72.8% (sample/judge-version unclear); human study 56.7% prefer human edit (Fig 4, App D)
code_available: project page ogatakatsuya.github.io/medit-bench; data = YouTube IDs + messages + cut timestamps; code/weights not confirmed
license: not stated in text; arXiv perpetual licence (paper only)
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Closest benchmark to ours in evaluation design: multi-reference, cut-level F1 at strict thresholds, and a documented FAILURE of an LLM judge vs humans; but it is visual-only, 1-3 min edits, no speech.

title: Timeline-Bench: Evaluating Agents on Realistic Video-Editing Tasks, from Raw Footage to Final Cut
authors: Gunin Gupta, Nirmit Arora, Pavan Kalyan Tankala
task_input: brief + raw assets
task_output: finished video
supervision_source: 3 multimodal-LLM judges calibrated on 2582 blind pairwise judgments by 43 professional editors (863 pairs, 3 editors each)
dataset_used_or_released: releases 56 tasks, verifier, per-run results
eval_metrics: resolution rate (all tests + quality test); human win-or-tie rate; quality test = 3-judge z-scored panel score vs reference with tie margin fitted to human win-or-tie rate, leave-one-agent-out
key_result_with_number: Judge validity: system-level (16 agents) rho=0.93 / r=0.93, mean gap 3.0 pts, max 7.2; single edit kappa=0.15 vs one human vs rest 0.14; per-task rho=0.32 (App D.4); single-judgment Krippendorff alpha 0.103; Spearman-Brown reliability 0.84; humans prefer reference 83.5%
code_available: code, task definitions, rubrics, frozen constants and results released under Apache-2.0 (App M); source media only for approved research teams
license: Apache-2.0 (code/tasks/rubrics/results); media access-restricted, no redistribution, no training on benchmark
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] Gives the only fully specified 'human-calibrated judge' recipe (tie margin fit to human win-or-tie rate, leave-one-agent-out) - valid for ranking systems, NOT for scoring individual edits.

title: VlogReward: Learning Multi-Dimensional Evaluation for Vlog Editing
authors: Yexiang Liu, Wen Zhong, Sijie Zhu et al.
link: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22632 (ICML 2026 poster page icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/61914; project VlogReward.github.io)
task_input: raw assets + MLLM-synthesised edit plan
task_output: 6-dimension scores (1-5) + textual feedback
supervision_source: SFT + GRPO with inter-group comparison reward; labels from MLLM scoring with human audit (3.6k person-hours)
dataset_used_or_released: releases VRMBench (400 groups x 4 plans = 1.6k) and 100k-edit training set
eval_metrics: Score accuracy (exact match on 6 dims), pairwise Comparison accuracy over 4 quality-ranked plans, Best-of-N accuracy; no human correlation
key_result_with_number: Table 1 VlogReward Comparison acc SB/OB/AVG 60.4/86.6/73.5, BoN 48.3/86.8/67.6, Score 45.9/56.7/51.3; Gemini-3-Pro SB comparison 60.5 (VlogReward barely above on subjective cases, chance 50); GPT-5 72.5 OB vs 53.7 SB; labels = MLLM scoring + human audit + synthetic tampering (shot timestamps/subtitles); no independent human agreement or inter-annotator number reported
code_available: project page VlogReward.github.io; code/data not confirmed; ethics statement says raw data should not be publicly distributed
reading_depth: full-text (arxiv.org/abs + html 2607.22632, Sec 1-5, Tables 1-3, App A/B)
one_line_takeaway: [CORE] NOT human-validated: ground truth is AI-assisted scoring + synthetic degradations; shows reward-model accuracy on constructed rankings, not agreement with viewers.

title: Learning to summarize from human feedback
authors: Nisan Stiennon, Long Ouyang, Jeff Wu et al.
task_input: Reddit post / CNN-DM article
task_output: summary
supervision_source: human pairwise comparisons -> reward model -> RL
dataset_used_or_released: TL;DR (123,169 posts) human-comparison set
eval_metrics: labeler-researcher and labeler-labeler agreement; reward-model agreement; human preference win rate
key_result_with_number: labelers agree with researchers 77+-2% (researchers with each other 73+-4%); RM agrees with labelers 62.4%/66.5% (1.3B/6.7B) on CNN/DM vs inter-labeler 66.9%; ROUGE agreement ~57% falls to ~50% on RL-model samples; RM prefers minimal human edits 79.4%/82.8% vs separate humans 84.1%
one_line_takeaway: Template for validating a learned preference model: report model-human agreement against human-human ceiling and show proxy metric (ROUGE) decouples under optimisation.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
authors: Lianmin Zheng, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ying Sheng et al.

task_output: pairwise verdict
supervision_source: 3K expert votes (MT-Bench) + 30K crowdsourced arena conversations
dataset_used_or_released: MT-Bench
eval_metrics: agreement with humans (with ties S1 / without ties S2); position, verbosity, self-enhancement bias
key_result_with_number: GPT-4 pairwise vs human agreement 66% (S1) / 85% (S2) vs human-human 63% / 81%; GPT-4 vs GPT-4 single 70%/97%
one_line_takeaway: Reference protocol and numbers for judge-human agreement incl. human-human ceiling and position-swap consistency; text-only.

title: TREC 2020 Podcasts Track Overview
authors: Rosie Jones; Ben Carterette; Ann Clifton et al.
task_input: Task1 segment retrieval: topic query -> relevant 2-min segments (1-min stride overlap, ~3.4M segments); Task2 summarization: episode transcript(+audio,+description) -> short standalone text summary
task_output: Ranked 2-min segments; short grammatical standalone text summary (phone-screen length)
supervision_source: NIST assessor graded judgments (PEGFB for retrieval; EGFB 4-2-1-0 plus 8 yes/no attribute questions for summaries); creator descriptions as ROUGE reference
dataset_used_or_released: Spotify Podcast Dataset (100k+ English episodes; Google ASR with 0.1s word timestamps; released with track)
modalities: ASR transcript; audio provided but not used by summarization participants; 1 retrieval team used audio only to improve ASR
eval_metrics: Retrieval: mean nDCG (also nDCG@30, P@10); Summarization: EGFB score, ROUGE-L vs creator description
key_result_with_number: Best retrieval nDCG 0.67 vs BM25 0.52; transcript text 0.58 vs title-only 0.22 nDCG; best summ EGFB 2.04 vs creator descriptions 1.45; ROUGE-L vs EGFB Pearson only 0.28; 15 teams
code_available: [V] dataset access via Spotify request; evaluation script released on TREC site (2021)
one_line_takeaway: Defines the podcast segment/summary evaluation protocol; evidence that ROUGE is a poor proxy for human quality and that audio was essentially unused in 2020

title: TREC 2021 Podcasts Track (task descriptions and overview)
authors: Jussi Karlgren; Rosie Jones; Ben Carterette et al.
task_input: Task1: retrieve 2-min segments for queries incl. non-topical targets (entertaining / opinionated / contains discussion); Task2: summarization plus submit an audio clip that gives the sound of the episode
task_output: Ranked segments; text summary + audio clip
supervision_source: NIST assessors judged segments using transcript AND audio on Perfect-Excellent-Good-Fair-Bad scale; summaries EGFB + ROUGE
dataset_used_or_released: Same 100k-episode corpus; 2021 test queries 59-108
eval_metrics: Segments: mean nDCG, nDCG@30, P@10 over PEGFB (assessors saw transcript + context + audio); summaries: EGFB 4-2-1-0 over 193 episodes + 8 boolean attributes + binary audio-clip acceptability; no inter-assessor agreement
key_result_with_number: Summarization quality (0-4)/audio acceptability: best PoliTO 1.06/0.98, first-minute baseline 0.81/0.96, Hotspot1 0.43/0.95; quality much lower than 2020 (best >2.0 then); retrieval topical best nDCG ~0.51-0.53, entertaining rerank best ~0.30-0.31; no with/without-audio ablation reported; PEGFB wording penalises segments that start without enough context (Fair)
reading_depth: full-text (12-page overview PDF via pdftotext; per-run tables partly garbled)
one_line_takeaway: 2021 added subjective targets (entertaining/opinionated/discussion) and an audio-clip output -- the only TREC-style setting that asks for audio-judged engagement

title: Transforming Podcast Preview Generation: From Expert Models to LLM-Based Systems
authors: Winstead Zhu; Ann Clifton; Azin Ghazimatin et al.
task_input: Episode transcript (timestamped sentences) + title + description; Gemini 1.5 Pro with few-shot prompt
task_output: One ~1-min contiguous preview segment: start/end timestamps at sentence boundaries ("self-contained moments easy to understand without additional context")
supervision_source: No trained labels; manually curated few-shot examples; offline pairwise human preference + Yes/No on understandability / contextual clarity / interest; online A/B

title: Unbiased Learning-to-Rank with Biased Feedback
authors: Joachims, Swaminathan, Schnabel

title: Position Bias Estimation for Unbiased Learning to Rank in Personal Search
authors: Wang, Golbandi, Bendersky et al.
task_input: click logs (email search, file-storage search; <=1 click/query)
task_output: ranker (lambdaMART w/ IPW) + position-bias estimate
supervision_source: clicks; position bias estimated from regular clicks by regression-based EM (no randomization) vs RandTopN / RandPair randomization
dataset_used_or_released: Google email + Drive search logs (proprietary)
eval_metrics: weighted MRR; click log-likelihood
key_result_with_number: RandPair-corrected beats NoCorrection by +2.14% (email) / +0.15% (file storage) MRR; EM-estimated propensity also gives significant gain; randomization hurts user MRR (Table 1)
one_line_takeaway: Position-bias model assumes P(click)=P(examine|position)*P(relevant|q,d); a factor model + regression-EM can recover propensity from observational logs without randomizing - closest to what we could do with heatmap data we cannot intervene on

title: Estimating Position Bias without Intrusive Interventions
authors: Agarwal, Zaitsev, Wang et al.
task_input: click logs from >=2 rankers (A/B or successive production rankers)
task_output: propensity curve estimate (Intervention Harvesting, AllPairs estimator)
supervision_source: clicks; natural interventions = same doc placed at different ranks by different rankers
dataset_used_or_released: arXiv full-text search (~53,000 queries/25,600 clicks over May-Aug 2018); Google Drive search; Yahoo LTR simulations
eval_metrics: propensity MSE; agreement with swap experiment
key_result_with_number: AllPairs within CI of gold-standard swap experiment with tighter CIs on arXiv search; robust to click noise; MSE rises sharply when propensity curve is steep
one_line_takeaway: Key requirement: query/item distribution must not depend on which ranker was used (Pr(Q|f)=Pr(Q)); the analogue for video would need the same content shown at different 'positions' under quasi-random assignment

title: Unbiased Learning to Rank with Unbiased Propensity Estimation (Dual Learning Algorithm)
authors: Ai, Bi, Luo et al.
task_input: click logs (no randomization)
task_output: ranker + propensity model learned jointly
supervision_source: clicks; propensity estimation formulated as dual of unbiased LTR (IPW on both sides)

eval_metrics: MAP, nDCG, ERR@10
key_result_with_number: DLA >10% ERR@10 improvement over UBM- and DBN-trained rankers on real data
one_line_takeaway: Joint learning of propensity and relevance from raw logs works without interventions, but identifiability needs the same item to appear at different positions/contexts and examination to depend only on position (PBM)

title: Unbiased Learning to Rank Meets Reality: Lessons from Baidu's Large-Scale Search Dataset
authors: Hager, Deffayet, Renders et al.
task_input: Baidu-ULTR click logs + expert annotations
task_output: evaluation of ULTR methods (IPS, two-tower, DLA, RegressionEM, PairD)
supervision_source: clicks (training), expert relevance labels (test)
dataset_used_or_released: Baidu-ULTR (reranking subset: ~1.8M train sessions, 11.7M query-doc pairs; 6985 annotated queries)
eval_metrics: DCG@10, MRR, click NLL
key_result_with_number: ULTR methods yield no or marginal gains in DCG@10 vs naive despite strong estimated position bias; choice of loss/features matters far more; better click prediction does not imply better ranking
one_line_takeaway: [CAUTION] Counterfactual debiasing helps clearly in simulation but not reliably on a real log; any debiasing of replay labels needs a human-labelled test set to show it helps

title: Deconfounding Duration Bias in Watch-time Prediction for Video Recommendation (D2Q)
authors: Zhan, Pei, Su et al.

dataset_used_or_released: Kuaishou production data; live A/B on Kuaishou App
eval_metrics: XAUC, XGAUC, MAE; live WatchTime
key_result_with_number: Res-D2Q with 30 duration groups best offline; live +0.746% WatchTime vs VR baseline (typical production gain ~0.1%)
one_line_takeaway: Duration confounds both exposure and watch time; stratify by duration quantile (backdoor adjustment) - directly transferable to clip-popularity labels where clip length confounds views/completion

title: Clicks can be Cheating: Counterfactual Recommendation for Mitigating Clickbait Issue
authors: Wang, Feng, He et al.

dataset_used_or_released: Tiktok micro-video (ICME 2019 challenge; caption=exposure features, audio/visual=content) and Adressa news
eval_metrics: NDCG@10, Precision@20 (w.r.t. post-click likes)
key_result_with_number: CR outperforms normal training (NT) by +11.11% N@10 on Tiktok and +7.47% on Adressa; larger gain as share of dislike-ending clicks rises
one_line_takeaway: Closest recsys analogue to 'title/thumbnail effect': model the direct exposure->click path and subtract it; needs content features separable from exposure features and a post-click satisfaction signal for evaluation
